utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought in, if I could mention to those present that in its decision of the 4th of March on the 65 ter exhibit list of the Prosecution, the Chamber reserved its decision in respect of document 22 because there wasn't an English translation. That translation has now been provided and document 22, as described in that decision, will now be added to the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I am Veljko Djurdjic, member of the Defence team for the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. Together with me today is Ms. Marie O'Leary, who's a member of our team; lead counsel Dragoljub Djordjevic is away on official business. The two of us speak the same language, so I'm going to ask you that we do not overlap so that we would make it possible for the interpreters to do their job properly. So please be careful. Start speaking once the transcript is typed out, and I'll try to do the same thing. May I call you Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have studied all the statements you gave, and there is something that caught my attention. You gave a statement to the investigators of the OTP from April 2005 until January 2006. Could you please explain this to me. How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, in April I gave a statement. I think that went on for two days, so that was on two occasions. Then we waited for the translation into Serbian. I think that was the time involved. Also, I think there was some kind of a mistake, whatever, something was lost, the sketch that I had drawn. And then, I mean -- well, I draw the sketch again. I think that that's what happened -- I mean that second time in 2006 -- was it 2006?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would be interested in the following now: The first two days when you gave your statement, I think that is what you said, did you sign the statement that you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't because it was in English. It's a language I don't understand, so I didn't want to sign that in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, six months later, what was it that you signed, what version?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The version in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that something got lost. Could you please explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the last page. It's a sketch. It's a sketch of the scene, just a sketch, a little drawing that I made. Now, was it lost? I don't know. I don't know what the explanation was exactly, but I did the exactly the way it had been the first time, and also there were some changes in terms of the translation that I disagreed with. I thought that the translation was not right. I mean, I wanted it to say what I had said, the way I had felt I had given my statement. So it was really a minor matters, nothing special. That was done then in Serbian, in the Serbian language, and I signed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the first time you saw the translation was in 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then you had some objections to raise in respect of the translation, or rather, the content of the statement that you had signed in Serbian; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I mean, there was something, I can't remember exactly now, it wasn't anything that was of essence, that would change matters drastically. Later on, for example, the gentlemen who were putting the questions to me did not realise what the difference was between "komandant" and "komandir," which is a major different in our language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to give me questions only if you had witnessed something personally, and if you don't know something, just say "I don't know." Also, if you don't understand me, just say that you don't understand me, and I'll try to rephrase my question, if I can. You were born in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that's where you completed your education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the reason why you didn't do your military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I completed the secondary school of the interior for police work in Zagreb, it is a four-year school; and within the curriculum there is military training, and that is later recognised as military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, when did you ultimately complete your education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1980 I completed my education and started working, and then I had a one-year specialised on-the-job training course in Zagreb. I think that was in 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you said to me 1980, you meant that that's when you completed the police secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And after that you completed an extra one-year school -- one-year course?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1986. It was a specialised course for crime technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that you did not complete a post-secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not complete a post-secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you read your statement correctly, the one -- or did you read it carefully, the one you signed in Serbian in January 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that there is this one part where they treat my school as a post-secondary school; however, that one-year course was treated as post-secondary training and perhaps that's the way it was phrased in the translation too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In view of your education and schooling, you were a non-commissioned officer in terms of your rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Had you completed a post-secondary school, you could have been a commissioned officer; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what year was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1991. I think it was on the 19th of August. There was an armed conflict in that area, around Daruvar, Pakrac. I came to work, and then the National Guards Corps, that's what they were called, they took me prisoner. They had taken the police station during the night, and then I was a prisoner there for three days. Let me not go into all the details now. At any rate, I was released afterwards. My family was already in Serbia, and then I went to Serbia as well. Of course, of course, that's when I lost my job -- I mean, that is the essence of your question, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that you no longer returned to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never been to Croatia since.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you then got a job at the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me in which organisational unit you got this job and where were the headquarters of this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got a job at the SUP of the city of Belgrade. How should I put this? It was the police Brigade, that was the unit, the organisational unit, where I got a job. It's part of the Belgrade police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time it was called the Brigade of the Milicija; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Milicija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And everything that you described here before you transferred to the SAJ was what happened in that unit; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was there for two and a half years roughly, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, what kind of vacancy announcement was this, an internal one or an external one for recruiting members of the SAJ at the time when you were recruited?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the SAJ changed its location. After being located at the airport, it transferred to the locality where it is to this day. Since it is a rather large facility, it was necessary to provide additional security and logistics. I applied through a friend of mine, a policeman. I asked to speak to the then-commander of the SAJ, Zivko Trajkovic. They ran some extra checks, and then I was admitted into the SAJ. So it was a simple decision that was made for my transfer from one organisational unit to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would be interested in whether this was an internal vacancy announcement, and how did you find out there would be this vacancy at the savage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where -- where did that happen? Where were you interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the MUP, where the command for the SAJ was, for all the special units of Serbia, in the office of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were other people admitted at the same time when you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were other people who were admitted at the time. It wasn't really in regular cycles. Say it was within a month or two, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And they were all interviewed before being admitted into the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, probably. I think that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You were already a policeman. You worked at the Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the Brigade of the Milicija in Belgrade. And tell me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Other microphones are on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So were you already a member of the police, and therefore did you have proper security, clearance, or was extra clearance needed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking informally now. I think that there was an extra security check because I don't know how much time had elapsed between my interview with Commander Trajkovic up until the moment when the decision was made for me to be admitted. But on the basis of the interview I had with Trajkovic, he asked me questions, like whether I had been a member of any paramilitaries, like Arkan's men or something like that. And since I came from Croatia, he said that if he ever found out that I was a member of any one of these units, that he would not tolerate that kind of thing and that he wouldn't really need me. He said that quite openly during the interview. I think that through certain people, I don't know, through the state security, whatever, but I imagine that they did run some kind of a check, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there such a unit in Croatia too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an identical unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would be interested in the following: You talk here about some history of this unit that I'm not actually aware of. At that time, were you aware of some history of this unit that you were being admitted into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was aware of it. That's what we learned. We learned about the origins of the unit in Croatia, Serbia, et cetera, how they came into being. They all came into existence roughly around the same time. They were established roughly around the same time. That was one of the questions, one of the questions within that proposal that was made when they presented the structure of the unit to me and the history of the unit. So roughly, that's what I talked about, although I found it a bit strange, I mean specifically in my case, the history of the unit, whatever, it's a generally known thing. But I did say what I said, yes. Perhaps I wasn't accurate enough in terms of the establishment of the unit -- well, you know, I'm not a historian, but I know that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You said that they were putting questions to you, people from Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's their table of the chain of command in the SAJ with the names, who was what. The late Radovan Stojicic and then further on, the structure of the SAJ, what it looked like, et cetera. I think that the objective was to see where I was in the chain of command, or rather, on that table. I think that that was the essence, but the names and surnames of all the people were written down there, people who held certain positions, and there was nothing for me to add or take away or deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how come you knew that this was a Human Rights Watch document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I was told as much. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that you reviewed the document and said that the structure as reflected therein was accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the schematics were quite faithfully reflected up from the main command down to the units. We had three units: Pristina, Belgrade, and Novi Sad SAJs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Radovan Stojicic and the fact that you saw his name there. Where did you see his name, as part of which structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was earlier on, at the time when he was one of the SAJ commanders. I believe I saw his name there. I may be mistaken, and I'm referring to the history as presented there of the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, you said that you saw the name of Radovan Stojicic, and you've just confirmed to us that he was an SAJ commander for a while there in that document. Tell me, please, were there other names of other SAJ commanders presented there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zivko Trajkovic, who replaced him as commander, and he remained the commander of all the SAJ units, of the entire SAJ throughout the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, the entire structure complete with names was presented to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, including the chain of command structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've just told me that there's a difference between "komandir" and "komandant" and you've already mentioned three SAJ units. You said that Mr. Trajkovic was in command of all these units. Who did you belong to in that structure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I belonged to the Belgrade SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you were first admitted there, where was your unit headquartered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Batajnica, the 13th of May neighbourhood, that's what it's called, and that's where it still remains today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that you went to work there, in Batajnica, and that's where you, in fact, did your job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if I understood you well, you said a moment ago that the headquarters of the entire unit -- of all the units was in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kneza Milosa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Kneza Milosa. Are you aware of the numbers of men and the structure of units there at Kneza Milosa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived and became a member of the SAJ, Trajkovic was the commander; there was his deputy and a secretary, a lady secretary, and a driver or a courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did Commander Trajkovic issue orders to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was far down the chain of command, and my immediate commanders issued orders to me --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please do not utter any names until I ask you to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, we have been skirting on the edge of information that might be better not broadcast, and I think we're now getting across the line. We had better move into private session if you're going to explore this a little further.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was just meaning to ask that we move into private session on the issue of the "komandirs."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that you were not present at the centre when the trucks were brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that your "komandir" informed you when it was that you were supposed to come to the centre, to the previous location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You do not have any direct knowledge about where the trucks had come from, come to the centre in Batajnica, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 35 you mention that a person was a member of the DB and that you talked to that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but this is simplified. I mean, they say here a guy from the Kosovo DB state security. I don't really know if such an organisational unit existed, the Kosovo DB. They really simplified this. There was a man there who was, say, 35, he came there with a Mercedes without licence plates. And he said, How are things going? I was angry because I had to do all these things and so on and so forth. And there was a bit of verbal conflict there and he said - I didn't write that out here - but he said, Watch out so that the darkness doesn't devour you. Those were his words. I never saw him after that. He had a longish -- or rather, he had a coat and longish hair. He was pretending to look like a detective, whatever, a sort of brash guy. Well -- but, everybody was dislocated at the time. There was no one in the area, not the military, no one. So from time to time people came to see -- he probably came there with a purpose. He was riding around in this car when this job was being done. I never actually found out who he was or what he was. This is just an assumption on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that you don't know whether these trucks on the road up to the base had an escort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know at all how they came, whether there was an escort and so on. I had very few contacts with the drivers, two or three maybe. And -- well, we didn't really discuss that, we really didn't have time to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see a driver in civilian uniform -- well, sorry about that, in civilian clothes, rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was this elderly man or middle-aged. I remember him because he came with a completely new truck, and it was supposed to be his very own truck, privately owned. So I wondered, I wondered that this kind of work was being done with a truck like that. But as I told you, there was state of war and there was not much choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, was the bombing intensive in that part of town, because that's where the airport is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the airport was bombed every day, unannounced, just like that. We used to say amongst ourselves -- well, when they had nowhere else to bomb, then they just load off all their bombs on the Batajnica airport. It was the usual thing, explosions out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that you burned tires in order to make it impossible for NATO aircraft to see where you were, so that they couldn't bomb you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. May I explain that in two sentences? When I went to Kosovo, I was surprised that by the bridges people were burning straw, tires, whatever, and then I asked someone down there, a soldier or someone, I said, Why are they doing that? And then someone explained that to me, that when there is a lot of smoke, when you burn, say, tires or wet straw or something, that that is a kind of mask -- or rather, that the pilot does not have visual contact from the air, that he cannot locate us. Since I worked with a machine that was very hot, then we did the same thing, and we said, Well, let's try to do that by way of - how should I put this? - some kind of protection or something. I think it was more of a psychological thing for us rather than any kind of real protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that the bodies that you buried in the pits were not burned, or rather, that you did not burn them in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that you received per diems when you went to Kosovo on official business and when you would stay there for a day or two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the usual thing. When you would leave the base, or rather, the place where you worked for over 12 hours, then the law gave you an entitlement, you were entitled to a per diem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that when you do any kind of job at the headquarters of your organisational unit, that you do not get any kind of compensation except for your actual salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just the regular salary. This is customary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right -- well, yes, I am right. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Neuner, do you re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just some very few questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked about the JSO today. Could you explain what the JSO is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: JSO you mean? That is special operations unit. That is an abbreviation, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who in 1999, if you know, commanded that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Lukovic, Milorad Ulemek or Milorad Lukovic, called Legija, that's what he's called. I don't really know what his real name is then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would you know to who Mr. Milorad Ulemek reported to in 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, theoretically, if they belonged to the state security sector, then probably to the head of the state security sector. If there was state security then -- well, there was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you don't know, you don't need to answer. Do you know who in 1999 was the head of the state security sector?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Radomir Markovic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were asked about the drivers who had brought the trucks to Batajnica, and you said - and that's on page 23 of today's transcript - that you had three to four contacts with these drivers. Could you tell me, when was your first contact with a truck driver bringing the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I met with two of them briefly. On that sketch, that is vehicle number 4. The people who came on that vehicle had a problem there, the truck broke down, and they had a fuel problem. So I sort of had a contact with them -- I mean, they had to take the truck back and so on and so forth. So then we had to organise the repair of the truck and -- well, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you tell me where did you meet them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over there, in Batajnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the base itself, yeah?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, the base itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And these two gentlemen, what were they wearing when you met them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your question. What they were wearing as in clothing or what they were carrying as in their hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What they were wearing -- what clothes they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blue police camouflage, it was the so-called intervention uniform that is used to this day, standard police uniform. Let me mention without short-barrelled weapons, let me say that -- or rather, they didn't have long-barrelled weapons or short-barrelled weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me how long were these drivers at the base, meaning at Batajnica base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were there very briefly. I think they were put up in town in one of our hotels. We have these police hotels. They were there for as long as the truck was being repaired and fuel provided for the trucks. So it went on, say, for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you mentioned some police hotels. Could you explain what you meant by this. Where were the drivers of the trucks staying during these two or three days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police hotel is the place where unmarried policemen would stay. It was like any other sort of hotel. It had rooms and a restaurant. I don't know if it was owned by the MUP or whether the MUP was renting the place. I don't know the details. At any rate, any guests we received would be accommodated there. We call it the hotel for single men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in which town was that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade. It is still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, you mentioned you had three to four contacts in your testimony. Could you explain to me -- you've just described one contact here with these two drivers. Where were the other two or three contacts? When were these contacts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the same drivers we were discussing before?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out whether you had these three to four contacts with these two gentlemen or with other drivers, since you mentioned in your testimony that there were a couple of trucks arriving.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We're discussing the two men who had difficulties with the truck. I exchanged a few sentences with them. This one individual who was there in civilian clothes, an elderly man, he had a new truck. And there was another driver who brought over a refrigerator truck; he was a younger man. If we are discussing any sort of socialising with them, well I exchanged a couple of words with them and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain to me -- you mentioned a refrigerator truck. Is that a truck which also contained bodies or another delivery was in it, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a trailer truck that was some 30 years old at the time. It is -- it can be termed as a refrigerator truck because it can transport refrigerated goods or any sort of goods. But what was exactly your question? It escaped me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On that occasion when you met this driver with the refrigerator truck, do you know what goods or what delivery were in the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me. When we opened it up, I saw that there were -- that it was a load full of soil, black soil, 3 to 4 cubic metres of it. The smell that came out of it reminded me of perhaps corpses, but I couldn't see any. It did surprise me, though, that such a large truck should be used to transport 3 cubic metres of soil only.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain to me what clothes was the driver of that refrigerator truck wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also wore a camouflage police uniform. I don't think he had -- he carried any weapons -- or at least I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have for a moment Exhibit 325 being displayed to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you have seen this photo-board earlier. If it comes up I would just ask you two questions. The first question is: If you remember, what were the clothes of the two drivers which you mentioned a moment ago. I'm not asking about the truck driver of the refrigerator truck. I'm asking about the two drivers of the first truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless I'm mistaken, the witness said that one of them wore civilian clothes, whereas all the others had the same type of uniform. So the question doesn't seem to be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the -- Mr. Neuner is attempting to have some identification of the uniform worn. That much seems relevant. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just tell me if you recognise any of the picture or any of the uniforms here. The two drivers where you stated a moment ago who had uniforms on, which of the numbers depicted here, if any, were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the last question is: The uniform worn by the refrigerator truck driver, if it resembles any uniform here, which number would it resemble?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, number 4, but he only had the shirt and trousers without the belt and the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questioning. We have also your statements and previous evidence to consider. We would like to thank you for your patience in being here so many days and for the assistance you've been able to give us, and you are now free to leave and return to your normal activities. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 11th day of March, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
